A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AVHBench study. Their main text, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the additions, relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original AVHBench evaluations, multimodal versus unimodal experiments, Video-LLaMA training ablations and VAST transfer results in Tables 1–4, alongside qualitative and attention-map analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds AVinstruct evaluations in Table 5, newer-model evaluations in Table S1 and annotation-error case studies.

M1.justification: The two-stage annotation pipeline, audio alignment through a Q-Former and linear layer, and Video-LLaMA LoRA fine-tuning remain unchanged. The training objectives, frozen components and LoRA configuration match across the appendices. Added evaluations and annotation examples do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: v2 adds AVinstruct for external audio-visual instruction and multiple-choice evaluation, supplementing the existing VAST captioning evaluation. AVHBench's four tasks and the training data sources are retained. Revised benchmark sample counts do not establish different task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C and Table S1 substantially expand the evaluated comparison set with Video-SALMONN, Video-LLaMA2 and Gemini-Flash for multimodal and unimodal testing, plus LLaVA-OneVision and Qwen2-Audio for unimodal testing. The original comparison methods remain in Tables 1–3.

E3.justification: Figure 2 and Section 3 revise the reported benchmark from 2,327 videos, 5,816 judgment QnAs and 1,238 captions to 2,136, 5,302 and 1,106, respectively, and remove explicit validation-set counts. v2's introduction retains the old totals, and the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. The added AVinstruct evaluation introduces ROUGE-L, BLEU-4 and multiple-choice accuracy under zero-shot transfer.

E4.justification: v2 extends modality-removal comparisons to newer models and alignment/LoRA ablations to AVinstruct. Appendix D.5 and Figure S6 add two annotation-error correction cases, examining a spurious visual tag and an incorrectly merged caption. Existing qualitative examples and attention-map analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, repeated-seed variability or statistical significance tests. Temperature-zero generation, up-to-five retries for nonbinary answers and annotation-agreement reporting are unchanged; the retries do not constitute a newly added uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for newer models and AVinstruct. Table S1 reports, for example, Gemini-Flash's 83.3% audio-driven video accuracy and Video-LLaMA2's 74.2% video-driven audio accuracy. Within the new AVinstruct experiment, accuracy is 43.6% for unmodified Video-LLaMA and 57.8% with alignment plus LoRA. Original Tables 1–3 and the retained AVHBench/VAST ablation scores are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions remain unchanged. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: AVHBench, its semi-automatic annotation pipeline, evidence of cross-modal hallucinations and improved robustness through alignment and fine-tuning. The added experiments support these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning multiple-object interactions, temporal reasoning, longer videos and speech content, while dropping v1's suggestion to explore data-independent mitigation. Appendix D.5 explains how noisy tags and misaligned captions propagate annotation errors and how human verification corrects them. The main interpretation of cross-modal interference remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a dataset-repository link and a proposed leaderboard maintenance plan in Appendix H; Appendix A's subset-archive and future full-release wording remains unchanged. It removes v1 Appendix C.6's disclosure of an expanded 7,327-video corpus. Training hyperparameters, hardware, prompts and answer-parsing details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the newer evaluated models, AVinstruct, additional metrics, temporal-question datasets and related hallucination research. The main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged. Publication updates for SMILE and BEAF concern works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 separates limitations from the conclusion, adds appendix sections for quantitative results, annotation errors and maintenance, and adds acknowledgments. It also makes limited wording, author and affiliation edits. Most existing explanatory prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 4 is reorganized, with its VAST columns moved into Table 5 alongside AVinstruct results. v2 adds Table S1 and Figures S6 and S9 for newer-model results, annotation corrections and the leaderboard. Existing qualitative, attention and dataset-statistics figures are retained, with some relocation and renumbering; the overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The added newer-model comparisons and AVinstruct transfer ablations broaden the empirical support beyond v1, while concrete annotation-error cases and more specific limitations improve transparency. The gains are qualified by inconsistent sample accounting: v2's introduction retains 5,816 QnAs and 1,238 captions, whereas Figure 2 reports 5,302 and 1,106, without explaining the relationship to the unchanged original results.
